analysis_tag_prefix.description: Alert Analysis tag prefix. An alert carrying it was analysed outside this Worker.

blocked_by_verdict.description: Matches of an approved decision that was not acted on, because an alert of its key has a true positive or inconclusive verdict.

candidates.description: Open untriaged alerts of the look-back that were checked.

capped.description: Matches left for the normal path because the decision reached its daily cap.

close_failures.description: Approved decisions whose alerts could not all be closed, or that could not be read before the close. Each decision counts once.

closed.description: Alerts closed by a decision. Always 0 unless the mode is `on`.

decisions_matched.description: Distinct decisions that matched an alert.

deferred.description: Decisions left for the next sweep because the step ran out of time.

excluded_by_severity.description: Matches the severity guard keeps with a human, not tagged.

held_in_shadow.description: Matches on a cloud key, an untrusted signer or a key with neither a signer nor a hash that `on` only tagged, as shadow does: the alert goes to analysis.

left_for_notes.description: Matches left untouched for the next sweep because the sweep had no notes left for them.

notes_missing.description: Alerts a decision closed or skipped that have no note: a failed write, or past the time limit.

out_of_time.description: The step stopped starting decisions or reading pages because its time was spent.

skipped.description: Alerts kept out of analysis by a dismissal. 0 unless `on`.

status.description: `off` when the flag is `off` (the default), `disabled` when the Context Engine is off in the space, `failed` when nothing could be matched.

tag_failures.description: Decisions whose alerts could not all be tagged, or, for a dismissal, that could not be read before the tags. Each decision counts once. Those alerts match again next sweep.

unsettled_decisions.description: Decisions whose alerts the sweep could not check or put back after it wrote to them: the decision could not be read again, or a revoke that landed in between could not be undone. The sweep leaves the alerts as they are, and they may still carry the decision tag, but that is not certain: a revoke that ran in the meantime can have taken the tag off an alert before the sweep closed it. If the decision was revoked, run the revoke again: it finds the alerts that still carry the tag. An alert that does not carry it is not found and needs a manual review.

would_close.description: Alerts a false positive decision matched.
